\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Unanimous Boolean functions]
\lean{FABL.IsUnanimous}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p045-b002}
\label{FABL.IsUnanimous}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction}
A Boolean function $f\colon\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ is unanimous if it returns $1$ on the
input whose coordinates are all $1$, and returns $-1$ on the input whose coordinates are
all $-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Permutation invariance of a function]
\lean{FABL.IsSymmetric}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p045-b002}
\label{FABL.IsSymmetric}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.permuteInput}
Let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to a type $eta$. The function
is symmetric if permuting the coordinates of any input leaves its value unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Count invariant under coordinate permutation]
\lean{FABL.positiveCoordinateCount_permuteInput}
\label{FABL.positiveCoordinateCount_permuteInput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.permuteInput, FABL.positiveCoordinateCount, FABL.signValue, FABL.sum_signValue_eq_two_mul_positiveCoordinateCount_sub}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\\pi$ be a permutation of the $n$ coordinates, and let $x\\in\\{-1,1\\}^n$. The
number of coordinates equal to $1$ in the vector whose $i$th coordinate is $x_{\\pi(i)}$
equals the number of coordinates equal to $1$ in $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetry and positive-coordinate count]
\lean{FABL.isSymmetric_iff_eq_of_positiveCoordinateCount_eq}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p045-b002}
\label{FABL.isSymmetric_iff_eq_of_positiveCoordinateCount_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsSymmetric, FABL.exists_permuteInput_eq_of_positiveCoordinateCount_eq, FABL.positiveCoordinateCount, FABL.positiveCoordinateCount_permuteInput}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\beta$ be any type, and let
$f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\beta$. The function is invariant under every permutation of its input
coordinates if and only if $f(x)=f(y)$ whenever $x$ and $y$ have the same number of
coordinates equal to $+1$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube. If there is a real number $a$ such that
$f(x)$ is the sign of $a+\sum_i x_i$ for every input $x$, with zero assigned the
positive sign, then $f$ is invariant under every permutation of its coordinates and is
monotone in the coordinatewise order.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be invariant under every permutation of its coordinates
and monotone in the coordinatewise order. Then there is a real number $a$ such that, for
every $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, $f(x)=1$ when $a+\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\ge 0$ and $f(x)=-1$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetric monotone functions are equal weight thresholds]
\lean{FABL.symmetric_and_monotone_iff_isEqualWeightThreshold}
\label{FABL.symmetric_and_monotone_iff_isEqualWeightThreshold}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsEqualWeightThreshold, FABL.IsEqualWeightThreshold.symmetric_and_monotone, FABL.IsSymmetric, FABL.isEqualWeightThreshold_of_symmetric_monotone}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a function from the $n$-dimensional sign cube to $\\{−1,1\\}$. The function
is invariant under every permutation of its input coordinates and is monotone in the
coordinatewise order if and only if there is a real number $a_0$ such that, for every
input $x$, $f(x)$ is $1$ when $a_0+\\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\\ge 0$ and $-1$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetric monotone odd Boolean functions]
\lean{FABL.may_theorem}
\label{FABL.may_theorem}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsSymmetric, FABL.canonicalCountInput, FABL.canonicalCountInput_mono, FABL.isSymmetric_iff_eq_of_positiveCoordinateCount_eq, FABL.majority, FABL.positiveCoordinateCount, FABL.positiveCoordinateCount_canonicalCountInput, FABL.positiveCoordinateCount_le, FABL.positiveCoordinateCount_negateInput, FABL.signValue, FABL.sum_signValue_eq_two_mul_positiveCoordinateCount_sub, FABL.sum_signValue_ne_zero_of_odd, FABL.thresholdSign, FABL.thresholdSign_of_neg, FABL.thresholdSign_of_nonneg}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be invariant under every permutation of its coordinates,
monotone in the coordinatewise order, and odd, meaning $f(-x)=-f(x)$ for every input
$x$. Then $n$ is odd and $f$ is the majority function: its value is the sign of the sum
of the coordinates, with a nonnegative sum assigned value $1$.
\end{theorem}
